analysis.title: Aerospace & Defense: Aerospace in Pictures
key_insights: Goldman's monthly aerospace data pack concludes the commercial aerospace end market remains fundamentally strong, with global air traffic on an upward trajectory despite Middle East contraction and temporary weakness in international passenger volumes.

IATA reported total air traffic down 0.5% yoy in September, mainly from contractions in Middle East and North American demand. GS had forecast +1.4% yoy growth for September. The global load factor was 83.2%, down 20bps from a year ago.

International air traffic rose 0.4% yoy in September after falling 0.9% in August. International passenger capacity rose 0.5% after being flat in August. Domestic passenger traffic fell 2.2% yoy and domestic capacity fell 1.3%.
Global airline forward scheduled capacity shows yoy growth of 1%, 2% and 3% for October, November and December, a steady reacceleration into year-end despite volatile jet fuel.

Freight: international freight traffic rose 9% yoy in September (August +5%) and freight capacity rose 3% (August flat). US inbound nominal air freight rates rose 25% yoy in September. The latest FedEx air cargo growth was 6% and UPS was -8% yoy.

Large commercial orders: Boeing reported 165 new orders and 0 cancellations in September. Airbus reported 17 new orders and 3 cancellations. GS says order campaigning remains robust for both growth and replacement, and net orders are consistent with prior mid-cycle periods.
Parked aircraft are 11.4% of the total fleet, up 10bps month over month, and nearing pre-pandemic levels. Cancellations as a share of backlog are below historical averages.
Boeing and Airbus continue to improve production cadence, but supply chain and product quality remain hurdles. Both have multiple years of growth runway before meeting demand.

Aftermarket: GS expects high growth and above-inflation price increases to persist on tight supply/demand and an aging fleet, even with temporarily higher fuel prices. Airline inventory growth is below aftermarket growth, suggesting little to no inventory stocking.
Brent crude and jet fuel prices are trending upward. Average US airline yields rose 12.0% yoy in 2Q26. Global airline industry operating profits are expected to decline in 2026.

Business jets: US bizjet ops rose 3% yoy in September (August +2%, July +7%). European ops rose 3% (August +1%, July -1%). Used inventory rose 1% sequentially to 6.7% of the active fleet, still below all of 2000-2019.
Business jet TTM revenue rose 7% yoy with book-to-bill near 1.5x in 2Q26. Regional jet bookings were muted and revenue rose 8% yoy in 2Q26. Secondary market transactions are down from peak levels.

Leading indicators: ISM is slightly above its historical average in September, and China PMI is slightly below its long-term average. GS expects Europe real GDP growth of about 1.1% and US real GDP growth of about 2.2% on average over the next 4 quarters.

GS top stock picks in the sector, all Buy-rated: Loar Holdings (LOAR), Woodward (WWD), Boeing (BA), TransDigm (TDG), GE Aerospace (GE), HEICO (HEI), Howmet (HWM), Arxis (ARXS), Ducommun (DCO), CAE (CAE.TO) and Embraer (EMBJ).

sector_views.rationale: The end market is fundamentally strong, with robust order activity, multi-year OEM growth runway and tight aftermarket supply/demand.
Flight hours and used inventory are stronger than pre-pandemic and leading indicators point to growth, but levels are off-peak and vary by company.
